\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خراب} (kharāb)}{خراب (kharāb)}]{\ur{خراب} (kharāb) — out of order; bad}

\label{lesson:UR-C407-kharab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a canopy, then the Urdu for a night's shelter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خراب}}
\textbf{\ur{خراب}} — \emph{kharāb} — \textquotedblleft{}out of order; bad\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کمرے} \ur{کا} \ur{پنکھا} \ur{خراب} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kamre kā pankhā kharāb hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fan in the room isn't working.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{kharāb}, \textquotedblleft{}ruin, desolation\textquotedblright{}; in Urdu a broken fan, spoilt food and bad weather are all \textbf{\ur{خراب}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kharāb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kharāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kamre kā pankhā kharāb hai.} — The fan in the room isn't working.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a canopy, then the Urdu for a night's shelter, then say \emph{kharāb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{خراب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Out of order; bad\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹوٹنا} (ṭūṭnā)}{ٹوٹنا (ṭūṭnā)}]{\ur{ٹوٹنا} (ṭūṭnā) — to get broken; to break}

\label{lesson:UR-C407-tutna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a night's shelter, then the Urdu for out of order.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹوٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹوٹنا}} — \emph{ṭūṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to get broken; to break\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کھڑکی} \ur{کا} \ur{شیشہ} \ur{ٹوٹ} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khiṛkī kā shīshā ṭūṭ gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The window pane has broken.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{گلاس} \ur{ٹوٹ} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh glās ṭūṭ gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹوٹنا}} (\emph{ṭūṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ṭūṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}is broken\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{truṭyati} (CDIAL 6065); \textbf{\ur{توڑنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}, is the form for breaking something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شور} (shor)}{شور (shor)}]{\ur{شور} (shor) — noise}

\label{lesson:UR-C407-shor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for out of order, then the Urdu for to get broken.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شور}}
\textbf{\ur{شور}} — \emph{shor} — \textquotedblleft{}noise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سڑک} \ur{کے} \ur{شور} \ur{سے} \ur{میں} \ur{سو} \ur{نہیں} \ur{سکی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{saṛak ke shor se maiṅ so nahīṅ sakī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I couldn't sleep for the noise from the road.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شور}} (\emph{shor}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{shor}, \textquotedblleft{}an uproar, a clamour\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مرمت} (marammat)}{مرمت (marammat)}]{\ur{مرمت} (marammat) — a repair}

\label{lesson:UR-C407-marammat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to get broken, then the Urdu for noise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مرمت}}
\textbf{\ur{مرمت}} — \emph{marammat} — \textquotedblleft{}a repair\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مستری} \ur{نے} \ur{پنکھے} \ur{کی} \ur{مرمت} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mistrī ne pankhe kī marammat kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mechanic repaired the fan.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مرمت}} (\emph{marammat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{marammat}, \textquotedblleft{}a mending\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\ur{مرمت} \ur{کرنا}} is to repair.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہٹانا} (haṭānā)}{ہٹانا (haṭānā)}]{\ur{ہٹانا} (haṭānā) — to move (something) aside; to remove}

\label{lesson:UR-C407-hatana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for noise, then the Urdu for a repair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہٹانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ہٹانا}} — \emph{haṭānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to move (something) aside; to remove\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہوٹل} \ur{والے} \ur{نے} \ur{کمرے} \ur{سے} \ur{پرانا} \ur{بستر} \ur{ہٹایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hoṭal vāle ne kamre se purānā bistar haṭāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The hotel man took the old bed out of the room.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{میز} \ur{ہٹائی}, \emph{us ne mez haṭāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہٹانا}} (\emph{haṭānā}) is built on \emph{haṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to move out of the way\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under \emph{haṭṭ}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 13943): this is the form for moving something else.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haṭānā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for noise, then the Urdu for a repair, then say \emph{haṭānā} again
\end{itemize}
